land.text: the previous Edo Kingdom of Igodomigodo (Ogiso rule), from which the Benin kingdom grew

predecessors.note: No dossier for Igodomigodo; the page dates neither the end of the Ogiso nor the first Oba (Eweka I).

land.text: Benin was absorbed into the British Niger Coast Protectorate after Benin City fell on 18 February 1897

successors.note: The Benin Territories Expedition of 1899 was mounted against holdouts (Benin Empire page).

capitals.name: Edo (Benin City)
capitals.note: 'The Kingdom of Benin's capital was Edo, now known as Benin City in Edo State, Nigeria.' Ewuare is credited with the great wall and a rebuilding of the palace in the fifteenth century (Ewuare page).

correction.text: the Edo city-state around Edo (Benin City), 'the former city-state' that Ewuare's reign enlarged from 1440

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The page's infobox span begins 1180 and the lead has the kingdom growing 'out of the previous Edo Kingdom of Igodomigodo around the 11th century AD'; it gives no extent before Ewuare. A 50 km circle round Benin City stands for the city-state (the Edo State outline would be about 43,000 km2, too large for a city-state).

correction.text: Ewuare's conquests: 'Tradition records Ewuare as capturing 201 towns and villages' in Ekiti, Ikare, Kukuruku, Eka and 'Igbo country' west of the Niger, with the eastern Yoruba towns of Akure and Owo

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Edo State, Ondo State (Akure, Owo, Ikare), Ekiti State and a 40 km circle on the west bank of the Niger at Onitsha/Asaba for the Igbo country. The Ewuare page gives no year for any conquest; 1440 is the accession (Benin Empire page: 'In 1440, Oba Ewuare ... came to power and expanded the borders of the former city-state'). The page gives no area; the union is about 60,000 km2.

correction.text: the height of Benin: Edo, Ondo, Ekiti and the Niger bank plus the Niger Delta peoples (Urhobo, Isoko, Ijaw, western Igbo), the Itsekiri coast excluded

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'At its height in the 16th century, Benin dominated trade along the entire coastline'; the page names Niger Delta peoples (Western Igbo, Ijaw, Itsekiri, Isoko, Urhobo) and Eastern Yoruba (Ondo, Ekiti, Mahin/Ugbo, Ijebu) as under Benin's sway, undated. Delta State minus a 30 km circle round Warri stands for them: the Warri page makes the Itsekiri kingdom sovereign (Bosman 1705: 'neighbour and ally'). Ijebu and Mahin/Ugbo are not drawn (tradition only). The page gives no area figure.

correction.text: Benin after the shrinking that followed Ehengbuda: the Ewuare core of Edo, Ondo, Ekiti and the Niger bank

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'Ruling in the late 16th century, Oba Ehengbuda was the last of the warrior kings;' the page says the empire shrank afterwards but does not say what was lost, so the shrink is drawn back to the Ewuare extent (confidence 1). Civil war c. 1689-1721 and the 1897 conquest follow; the page gives no extent for 1625, only a map caption 'The extent of Benin in 1625'.

ledger.note: 1180: the Edo city-state under its Oba. 'It grew out of the previous Edo Kingdom of Igodomigodo around the 11th century AD'; the infobox span reads 1180-1897. The page does not date Eweka's coronation or the first Oba.

region.text: Akure, Owo, Ikare and Ekiti towns

ledger.counterpart: Akure, Owo and the Ekiti town-states
ledger.note: 1440: Ewuare the Great begins the conquests. 'In 1440, Oba Ewuare ... came to power and expanded the borders of the former city-state' (Benin Empire page); the Ewuare page: 'Tradition records Ewuare as capturing 201 towns and villages' in Ekiti, Ikare, Akure, Owo; undated, within his reign c. 1440-c. 1473.

region.text: Kukuruku (northern Edo), Eka (Ika) and the Igbo country west of the Niger

ledger.note: 1440: Ewuare takes the western Igbo, Ika and Kukuruku villages. 'Tradition records Ewuare as capturing 201 towns and villages in' Ekiti, Ikare, Kukuruku, Eka and 'Igbo country' west of the Niger; no year on the page.

region.text: the Niger Delta peoples: Western Igbo, Ijaw, Isoko and Urhobo (Delta State without the Itsekiri coast)

ledger.counterpart: Delta peoples (Urhobo, Isoko, Ijaw and western Igbo)
ledger.note: 1517: Esigie beats the Igala and extends Benin east and south. 'In the early 16th century, Oba Esigie expanded the kingdom eastwards, after defeating an invasion' (Benin Empire page); the Esigie page dates the Igala war 'between approximately 1515 and 1517' (Curnow: 1519-1521) and says the victory 'reinforced the Oba's influence in the Niger region'. The Delta peoples are the page's 'under Benin' list at its 16th-century height, undated.

region.text: the outer Delta lands won under Esigie, no longer held after the shrinking (page silent)

ledger.counterpart: Delta peoples (Urhobo, Isoko, Ijaw and western Igbo)
ledger.note: 1600: the warrior kings end and the empire shrinks. 'Ruling in the late 16th century, Oba Ehengbuda was the last of the warrior kings;' after which the empire shrank. Page silent on what was lost and when; 1600 is a bridging year and the land is the 1517 gain.

region.text: Eko (Lagos), whose ruler Ashipa was appointed by the Oba of Benin and paid tribute

ledger.note: c. 1630: Eko (Lagos) is a tributary of Benin. 'The Oba of Benin appointed him [Ashipa] as ruler of Eko'; Ashipa 'initiated a payment of tribute that would not be abolished until 1830' (History of Lagos page); the Oba of Lagos list has Ashipa 1600-1630 ('not crowned') and Ado, first crowned king, from 1630. Reviewer af-04-x (2026-10-19): added as the mirror of kingdom-of-lagos 1630 (same year as that dossier's start).

c. 1830: Lagos stops paying tribute to Benin: tribute 'would not be abolished until 1830' (History of Lagos page); 'Eko's subservience to Benin was mostly nominal by the 18th century'. Reviewer af-04-x (2026-10-19): added as the mirror of kingdom-of-lagos 1830.

region.text: the road from the Niger Coast Protectorate to Benin City

ledger.note: 1897 (9 February): the British invade Benin. 'On 9 February 1897, the invasion of the Kingdom of Benin began' after Phillips' party was destroyed near Ugbine on 4 January.
1897 (18 February): Benin City falls. 'The capital was captured on 18 February.' Fire burnt the palace; the Oba was later 'deposed and exiled ... to Calabar'.

1897 (18 February): the kingdom passes to the British. 'Benin was absorbed into the British Niger Coast Protectorate and eventually into British colonial Nigeria'; a further 'Benin Territories Expedition' followed in 1899 against holdouts (Benin Empire page).

region.text: the Benin kingdom, to the Niger Coast Protectorate

ledger.note: 1897 (February): the Benin Empire ends with the fall of Benin City; Oba Ovonramwen died in exile at Calabar in January 1914 and his son was enthroned as Eweka II on 24 July 1914, who 'rebuilt the royal palace, which had been destroyed in 1897'.

wars.name: Benin-Igala war of Esigie
wars.outcome: Benin defeated the Igala invasion; 'the victory altered Benin's relationship with Idah and reinforced the Oba's influence in the Niger region' (Ryder, via the Esigie page).
wars.note: Dated 'approximately 1515 and 1517' by several reconstructions, 1519-1521 by Curnow, 'around 1517' for the defeat of Idah by Mowah. The page names no battlefield and no land that changed hands, so no contest zone is drawn; the Benin Empire page has the Igala invading and Esigie then expanding eastwards.

wars.name: Benin civil war
belligerents: Ozuere and the Iyase Ode (rival claimants)
wars.outcome: Civil war 'around 1689, around the time that Oba Ewuakpe ascended'; it lasted about ten years before negotiations, and Akenzua's side 'eventually prevailed over the younger Ozuere and his ally, the Iyase Ode in a decisive battle in 1721'; about ten more years went on cleaning up rebel areas.
wars.note: No land is named, so no zone or loss is drawn.

wars.name: British Benin Expedition
wars.outcome: British victory: 1,200 troops under Sir Harry Rawson captured Benin City on 18 February 1897; the kingdom was absorbed into the Niger Coast Protectorate; a Benin Territories Expedition in 1899 cleared holdouts.
wars.note: Phillips' party of about 250 was ambushed near Ugbine/Gwatto on 4 January 1897; invasion 9 February; capital captured 18 February. Reviewer af-04-x (2026-10-19): end set to 1897 (Benin Expedition of 1897 infobox: 9-18 February 1897), inside the dossier life; the 1899 Benin Territories Expedition against holdouts came after the kingdom ended.

certainty.note: No page gives a frontier line for the kingdom; the extents are the researcher's reading of lists of conquered towns and peoples. The Benin Expedition page marks no border.

sources.title: Benin Empire
sources.note: Identity, capital, 1180-1897 span, Ewuare 1440, Esigie, decline, civil war 1689-1721, 1897 and aftermath; no area figure on the page (infobox caption only: the extent of Benin in 1625).

sources.title: Ewuare
sources.note: Reign c. 1440-c. 1473; the 201 towns in Ekiti, Ikare, Kukuruku, Eka and western Igbo country; Akure and Owo; the walls (undated); Itsekiri accept Iginua.

sources.title: Esigie
sources.note: Reign c. 1504-1550 (or 1515/1517-1550/1566); Igala war c. 1515-1517; influence on the Niger; Portuguese contact 1514-1516.

sources.title: Benin Expedition of 1897
sources.note: 4 January ambush, 9 February invasion, 18 February capture, Oba exiled to Calabar, absorbed by the Niger Coast Protectorate.

sources.title: Warri Kingdom
sources.note: Itsekiri kingdom founded c. 1480 by Ginuwa, son of Oba Olua of Benin; sovereign, Benin an ally (Bosman 1705); protectorate treaty 1884; used to leave the Itsekiri coast out of the 1517 keyframe.

sources.title: History of Lagos
sources.note: Ashipa appointed ruler of Eko by the Oba of Benin; tribute to Benin until 1830 (added by reviewer af-04-x).

notes: Benin has no Cliopatria row. The pages opened (5, the budget) give no frontier and no area; every keyframe is a reading of lists of towns and peoples, so all borders are soft. Disagreements: Ewuare's reign c. 1440-c. 1473 (Egharevba/Sandomirsky) vs 1440-1481 (Millar); Esigie from 1504, 1515/1517 or 1517 and to 1550 or 1566; the Igala war c. 1515-1517 vs 1519-1521. The Benin Empire page lists the Itsekiri among Benin's subjects but the Warri page makes Warri sovereign and Ginuwa a Benin prince who founded it c. 1480 (migration 'began around 1470' on the same page); the dossier leaves Warri out and the Warri Kingdom needs its own dossier. Not placed (page silent): Ijebu, Mahin/Ugbo and a town near Lagos (a 1603-04 attack with European cannon is on the page without the attacker's name); the Lagos/Eko tie to Benin is not on any page opened. The 'shrinking' after Ehengbuda is a confidence-1 loss. Rulers omitted: the pages give no complete list with reign years (Ewuare, Esigie, Ohuan d. 1641, Ewuakpe c. 1689, Akenzua, Ovonramwen). Counterpart slugs without a dossier in this batch: igodomigodo (Ogiso kingdom, to 1180), igala-kingdom (Idah).
